title: Shmuel Saba, son-in-law of Rabbi Chanina

paragraphs: Shmuel Saba, son-in-law of Rabbi Chanina.

He is mentioned in [Berakhot 62b](https://www.sefaria.org/Berakhot.62b): he said in the name of Rabbi Chanina, “from the time of the slaughtering of the daily offering,” whereas Rabbi Yochanan said, “until precisely midday.” From this we see that he was the son-in-law of Rabbi Chanina bar Chama, Rabbi Yochanan’s teacher. If so, this is not Shmuel Saba, the father-in-law of Rav Shmuel bar Ami mentioned in Sotah 10; see the entry “Shmuel the Elder.”[^1]

notes.text: The heading explicitly calls him Rabbi Chanina’s son-in-law. His identification with Rabbi Chanina bar Chama and the distinction from the other Shmuel Saba are Hyman’s reasoning, preserved with “from this we see” and “if so”; no external identity is assigned. Saba remains a name element distinct from the separately cross-referenced title “the Elder.” The printed Berakhot locator סב: is conventionally 62b. Sotah is printed י; and supplies no a/b side; none is added. The quoted rulings are excerpts, not supplied complete discussions.
